transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, um… thanks for seeing me. I guess the main thing is I’ve been getting pulled off track really easily. Like, I’ll be trying to finish a dashboard, and then one Slack ping or even a song lyric or a random idea for some other project pops up, and suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread. It’s not… terrible all the time, but it’s been enough that I thought I should probably ask about it.

Thinking back, do you remember having this kind of trouble staying focused and getting easily distracted back when you were a kid or teenager, or is this something that's really only shown up recently?

Yeah, I think it’s been there for a long time… not just recent. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a “bad kid” or anything, because I wasn’t trying to be difficult, but even in elementary school teachers would write little comments about me rushing through worksheets or losing track of the directions.

And I guess group work was a thing too — I’d sometimes talk over people without meaning to. My parents also had to sit next to me during homework a lot, because if they didn’t I’d kind of wander off or start doing something else before I’d actually finished. So… yeah, I think it goes back pretty far, if that helps.
Besides the trouble staying focused, do you often feel physically restless or fidgety, like needing to move your legs, get up frequently, or feeling like you can't sit still for long periods?

Yeah… I mean, not in a super dramatic way, I don’t think. But if I have to sit still through a long Zoom call, or just work quietly in the same spot for a while, I start getting this kind of uncomfortable pressure in my body, like I need to get up or pace around or do something with my hands.

I can usually hold it together, I think, but it takes effort. Does that count as restlessness?
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers before someone finishes a question, interrupting conversations, or having trouble waiting your turn in situations like lines or discussions?

Um… yeah, a little. I don’t think I’m trying to be rude, but it does happen.

Like when people are brainstorming, I’ll get excited and blurt out my idea before they’ve really finished explaining theirs. Or I might start adding something to the Figma board while they’re still talking it through. And then afterward I realize it probably came off kind of pushy, even though in the moment I was just enthusiastic. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say these attention and restlessness issues have actually caused real problems for you—like at work, in your relationships, or in other parts of your daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say it’s not a huge deal, because I do try really hard to make up for it. But it has caused problems.

I’ve lost a couple of small freelance-type contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly enough, or people felt like they couldn’t totally rely on me. And there was a portfolio competition I missed out on because I didn’t get everything together the way I was supposed to.

It’s embarrassing to say, because I don’t want it to sound like I don’t care. I do care. But I think some friends or collaborators are a little hesitant to work with me now, even though they like my ideas. Does that make sense?
